(p-509) Surah al-'Asr is Makkan, and it has three verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿By the time (al-'asr)﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

This surah is Makkan according to Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and the majority, and Madinan according to Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil. When He said in the preceding surah: ﴿Competition in increase diverts you﴾ [at-Takathur: 1], and the threat came through the repetition of ﴿No! You will soon know﴾ [at-Takathur: 3], He then made clear the state of the believer and of the disbeliever.

﴿By the time (al-'asr)﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: It is time (ad-dahr). It is said of it 'asr, 'isr and 'usr. He, Exalted is He, swore by it because of the various kinds of wonders in its passing. Qatadah said: al-'Asr is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy). He swore by it as He swore by the forenoon (ad-duha), because of the signs of His power in both. It is also said: al-'Asr is the day and the night, and from this is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr:

The two 'asrs (day and night) will not remain a day and a night, if they seek to overtake what they have aimed for.

It is also said: al-'Asr is the early morning and al-'Asr is the evening, and they are the two cool times (al-abradan). On this view, and the one before it, the oath is by one of the two, not specified. Muqatil said: al-'Asr is the Middle Prayer, and He swore by it. Al-Zamakhshari began with this view. He said: because of its excellence, as evidenced by His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and the Middle Prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238], which in the mushaf of Hafsah reads "the 'Asr prayer", and by his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever misses the 'Asr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his wealth." This is because the burden of performing it is heavier, given people's rush in their trade, their settling of accounts at the end of the day, and their preoccupation with their livelihoods. End of quotation.

Sallam recited ﴿والعَصْرِ﴾ with a kasrah on the sad, and "bi-s-sabir" with a kasrah on the ba'. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is not permissible except when pausing, by transferring the vowel. It is related from Abu 'Amr: "bi-s-sabr" with a kasrah on the ba' as an ishmam (partial vowel indication), and this too can only be in pausing. End of quotation. In al-Kamil by al-Hudhali: "wa-l-'isr, wa-s-sibr, wa-l-fajr, wa-l-witr," with a kasrah on the letter before the sakin in all of these, is from Harun and Ibn Musa from Abu 'Amr, while the rest read with sukun, like the majority. End of quotation. Ibn Khalawayh said: ﴿وتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ with transfer of the vowel is from Abu 'Amr. The author of al-Lawami', 'Isa of Basra, said: "bi-s-sabir," by transferring the vowel of the ra' to the ba', so that one need not bring part of the vowel in pausing, nor make it sakin and thereby join two sakin letters. That is a widespread dialect, not irregular but well attested. It is an indication of the case ending (i'rab), and a way of avoiding the meeting of two sakin letters, though the basic rule for what is paused upon is sukun. End of quotation. In Sharh at-Tashil we cited several verses as evidence for this, such as the saying of the rajaz poet:

I am Jarir, my kunyah is Abu 'Amir; I strike with the sword while Sa'd is in the 'asir.

He means: Abu 'Amr, and al-'asr.

Al-insan (mankind) is a generic noun that is all-inclusive, and for that reason the exception from it is sound. Al-khusr is al-khusran (loss), like al-kufr and al-kufran. And what loss is greater than that of one who has lost this world and the Hereafter? Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd ibn 'Ali, and Harun from Abu Bakr from 'Asim recited "khusur" with a dammah on the sin, while the majority recited with sukun. Whoever sells his Hereafter for his worldly life is at the utmost extreme of loss, unlike the believer, who has bought the Hereafter with this world, and so has profited and been made happy.

﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾: that is, to the established matter, from those who act upon it and enjoin it upon one another. ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾: in obedience to Allah, Exalted is He, and in refraining from acts of disobedience.
